scope: Adults only (age 18 and over, age known). Under 18 or age unknown: no label (paediatric norms are out of scope). Blood pressure is not classified in pregnancy (pregnancy has its own definitions). Labels sit beside NEWS2 in the clerking desk's context panel; they never change NEWS2.

conventions.bands: Ordered low to high. A band with `from` starts at that value (≥); a band with `above` starts above it (>); the first band has no lower bound. A value takes the last band it reaches.
conventions.bpCategories: Ordered low to high. Each axis (systolic, diastolic) reaches the highest category whose threshold it meets (`systolicFrom` ≥, `systolicAbove` >, likewise diastolic). A category with no threshold on an axis cannot be reached by that axis. The reading takes the higher of the two axes' categories (the higher-category rule, quoted per scheme). Both values are needed.

tones.critical: Red: a genuine emergency only. Always printed with its words.

source.title: 2017 ACC/AHA/AAPA/ABC/ACPM/AGS/APhA/ASH/ASPC/NMA/PCNA Guideline for the Prevention, Detection, Evaluation, and Management of High Blood Pressure in Adults (Whelton PK et al. Hypertension 2018;71:e13–e115; J Am Coll Cardiol 2018;71:e127–e248)
source.section: Table 6 'Categories of BP in Adults'; section 11.2 hypertensive crises
source.verified: Cut-offs as given by the CSO brief and matched against secondary summaries; the publisher page refused retrieval (403), so the primary text was not quoted. Verify against Table 6 before signing.
source.higherCategoryRule: Table 6 footnote: individuals with SBP and DBP in 2 categories should be designated to the higher BP category.

source.title: 2018 ESC/ESH Guidelines for the management of arterial hypertension (Williams B, Mancia G et al. Eur Heart J 2018;39:3021–3104)
source.section: Table 3 'Classification of office blood pressure and definitions of hypertension grade'
source.verified: Table and footnotes retrieved from the publisher page 2026-10-08. The 2023 ESH guideline (J Hypertens 2023;41:1874–2071) was not retrieved; the brief says its table is unchanged: confirm before signing.
source.quote: Optimal <120 and <80 | Normal 120–129 and/or 80–84 | High normal 130–139 and/or 85–89 | Grade 1 hypertension 140–159 and/or 90–99 | Grade 2 hypertension 160–179 and/or 100–109 | Grade 3 hypertension ≥180 and/or ≥110 | Isolated systolic hypertension ≥140 and <90
source.higherCategoryRule: Footnote: "BP category is defined according to seated clinic BP and by the highest level of BP, whether systolic or diastolic." "Isolated systolic hypertension is graded 1, 2, or 3 according to SBP values in the ranges indicated."

source.title: 2020 International Society of Hypertension Global Hypertension Practice Guidelines (Unger T et al. Hypertension 2020;75:1334–1357; J Hypertens 2020;38:982–1004)
source.section: Classification of hypertension based on office BP
source.verified: Cut-offs as given by the CSO brief and matched against secondary summaries (AAFP 2021 summary of the ISH guideline: grade 1 below 160/100, grade 2 any higher); the primary text was not retrieved (publisher 403). Verify before signing.
source.higherCategoryRule: The table's "and/or" wording; an explicit footnote was not retrieved. Applied as for ESC/ESH.

source.title: Uganda Clinical Guidelines 2023: National Guidelines for Management of Common Health Conditions (Ministry of Health, Uganda)
source.section: 4.1.6 Hypertension, 'Classification of blood pressure (BP)', printed page 310 (PDF page 376)
source.verified: Quoted verbatim from the PDF text layer (UCG-2023-Publication-Final-PDF-Version-1.pdf), 2026-10-08.
source.quote: Classification of blood pressure (BP) | Category Sbp Mmhg Dbp Mmhg | Normal <120 and <80 | Pre-hypertension 120-139 or 80-89 | Hypertension, stage 1 140-159 or 90-99 | Hypertension, stage 2 >160 or >100
source.higherCategoryRule: Not stated in UCG; the table's "or" wording places a reading in a category when either value is in range, so the higher category applies.
source.gap: CSO ruling needed: UCG prints stage 2 as ">160 or >100", so 160 mmHg systolic and 100 mmHg diastolic fall in no row (stage 1 ends at 159 and 99). Implemented as ≥160 / ≥100, closing the gap upward as JNC 7 (the table's evident origin) does.

source.title: American Heart Association, patient information: Tachycardia (fast heart rate) and Bradycardia (slow heart rate)
source.verified: Cut-offs as given by the CSO brief (resting adult rate 60–100). The page refused retrieval (403), so no quote. Note for the CSO: the 2018 ACC/AHA/HRS bradycardia guideline defines sinus bradycardia as below 50/min, and NEWS2's zero band is 51–90.

source.title: Royal College of Physicians. National Early Warning Score (NEWS) 2: Standardising the assessment of acute-illness severity in the NHS. London: RCP, 2017 (chart 1: respiration rate 12–20 scores 0)
source.verified: Normal is NEWS2's zero-score band (lib/triage/constants.ts NEWS2_RESP_RATE). The words bradypnoea and tachypnoea are the brief's; NEWS2 does not name them.

source.title: Uganda Clinical Guidelines 2023, 1.4 Hypoxaemia Management and Oxygen Therapy Guidelines, 'Interpreting pulse-oximetry results', printed page 89 (PDF page 155); WHO threshold for oxygen therapy SpO₂ <90%
source.verified: UCG quoted verbatim: "SpO2 > 90% without danger signs = Normal | SpO2 < 90% =Low oxygen concentration in blood (Hypoxaemia) | SpO2 < 94 % with danger signs = Low oxygen concentration in blood (Hypoxaemia". The 95% lower edge of Normal is the brief's and is not in UCG (UCG calls >90% normal without danger signs, and <94% hypoxaemia with them): CSO to confirm the 90–94 caution band.

source.title: Royal College of Physicians. NEWS2, 2017: SpO₂ scale 2 for a prescribed target of 88–92% in hypercapnic respiratory failure (with BTS oxygen guideline 2017)
source.verified: Target 88–92% as on the NEWS2 chart (lib/triage/constants.ts NEWS2_SPO2_SCALE2*). Used only when the clinician set the 88–92% target or scale 2 in the examination.

source.title: Hypothermia: core temperature below 35 °C (Brown DJA et al. Accidental hypothermia. N Engl J Med 2012;367:1930–8). Raised from 37.5 °C: Uganda Clinical Guidelines 2023, 2.5.2.1 Uncomplicated malaria, printed page 165: "Fever: above 37.5°C (taken from the axilla)". Fever 38.0 °C: the examination catalogue's operational CSO value (REF-EX-FEVER-TEMP: Uganda VHF surveillance uses > 38 °C).
source.verified: Bands as given by the brief. CSO to rule: UCG calls above 37.5 °C fever (axillary), which this scheme labels 'Raised' until 38.0. Hyperpyrexia is not implemented: UCG's only figure (>39.5 °C) is a severe-malaria criterion with parasitaemia, and no general adult source for >40 °C was found.

source.title: 6. Glycemic Goals, Hypoglycemia, and Hyperglycemic Crises: Standards of Care in Diabetes—2026 (Diabetes Care 2026;49(Suppl 1):S132–S149), Table 6.4 'Classification of hypoglycemia', as quoted in data/ncd/diabetes-pack.json (DM-ACU-ROUTE-06, REF-DM-HYPO-L2) and the examination catalogue (REF-EX-HYPO-L1/L2)
source.quote: Level 1: Glucose <70 mg/dL (<3.9 mmol/L) and ≥54 mg/dL (≥3.0 mmol/L) | Level 2: Glucose <54 mg/dL (<3.0 mmol/L)
source.verified: Only the context-free bands: the pack's 'interpretation' glucose bands are glycaemic-control targets for a person with diabetes (At target / Above target) and are not applied to an unselected patient. A meter LO acts as level 2 (pack DM-ACU-ROUTE-06: 'a meter reading LO … Act now'); a meter HI is critical per the brief (beyond the meter's range). No label at 3.9 and above.

signoff.decision: Sign as listed; ACC/AHA 2017 is the default BP scheme.
rulings: Temperature: 38.0 °C is Fever (the clerking examination's signed fever line); 37.5–37.9 reads Raised, not UCG's 'above 37.5 = fever'.
UCG 2023 Stage 2 printed as '>160 or >100': exactly 160 or 100 is Stage 2 (as JNC 7).
ACC/AHA 2017 and ISH 2020 rows were checked against secondary summaries; the publishers' pages could not be fetched.
